strategy.summary: Build pandas at buggy commit 23f61296bcbf from source on Python 3.12.4 with NumPy 2.2.1 (issue-inferred, not README-documented), then run the three new uint64 tests in test_to_datetime.py and test_to_timedelta.py. The transition: on the buggy revision the scalar to_datetime(uint64_max, unit='ns', errors='raise') call returns a wrapped timestamp instead of raising, so pytest.raises fails with DID NOT RAISE; on the fixed revision the scalar and array raises and the coerce/valid cases hold. Message-match strings in the developer test are a real risk that could block the fixed-side pass.

pinned_because: numpy==2.2.1: era-inferred from issue#60677 only; no README constraint exists, so this is a choice made by the strategy, not a documented requirement
pandas 2.2.3 from issue#60677 is not installed as a dependency because the repository at the buggy commit is the code under test; it serves only as an era reference
python-dateutil, tzdata, Cython, NumPy: README-documented but unconstrained; left unpinned apart from the NumPy era choice above

strategy.success_criterion: Buggy revision: test_uint64_to_datetime_raise_oob and test_uint64_to_timedelta_raise_oob FAIL, because the scalar call to_datetime(uint64_max, unit='ns') (or to_timedelta equivalent) returns a wrapped value (1969-12-31 23:59:59.999999999 for datetime) rather than raising, giving 'DID NOT RAISE'. Fixed revision: the same tests PASS, with array and scalar raises matching and coerce yielding NaT and valid uint64 equal to the int64 result. The transition is the whole criterion.
strategy.numerical_probe: np.iinfo(np.uint64).max is 2**64-1; cast to int64 wraps to -1, which is 1969-12-31 23:59:59.999999999 under ns datetime; this explains the buggy output.

input_output_examples.buggy_output: raises 'cannot convert input 18446744073709551615 with the unit 'ns', at position 0'

risks: Message-match risk: the developer test matches 'cannot convert input with unit ns' (lowercase, no value), while the existing array message is 'cannot convert input 18446744073709551615 with the unit ns, at position 0'; the regex may not match and the fixed revision could fail the test anyway.

Timestamp and Timedelta match strings ('Out of bounds nanosecond timestamp', 'Cannot cast .* from ns to ns without overflow') are unverified against the fixed code and may need the exact upstream message.
The to_datetime code path fix is not shown in the evidence (only the to_timedelta diff); the scalar to_datetime expectation is inferred from the issue text, not from a diff.
Behaviour depends on uint64 to int64 wrap on the build platform; it is expected on any 64-bit platform but was not confirmed on a specific architecture, so no platform-specific claim is made.
A source build needs a C/C++ compiler and meson toolchain; these are not stated in the evidence and are assumed.
numpy==2.2.1 is an era-inferred pin from issue#60677, not a documented constraint; a different NumPy 2.x may change scalar uint64 handling and should be tried if the buggy side does not reproduce.
PR date is blank, so the exact era of the buggy commit is not confirmed beyond the issue reference.

oracle.why: Expected results are integer-valued ns timestamps and NaT; equality is exact, and the valid-uint64 case compares against the int64 cast result.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: On the buggy revision the array raise assertion may already pass (the array path raises). The scalar to_datetime(uint64_max, unit='ns', errors='raise') call returns 1969-12-31 23:59:59.999999999 without raising, so pytest.raises reports DID NOT RAISE OutOfBoundsDatetime, making the test fail.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: On the fixed revision the array and scalar calls raise OutOfBoundsDatetime/OutOfBoundsTimedelta and match the test's message regex, coerce returns NaT, and the valid uint64 case equals the int64 result, so all tests pass provided the message regexes match the fixed messages.
